characters.detention: Searched from Thomas Graves's Belongings: Tonight's handwritten note: '8:40 PM — Poured hot cup of chamomile tea in Study. 8:42 PM — Watched Chef Henri Laurent hand Arthur a signature dark-chocolate truffle in the Grand Hall. 9:02 PM — Tea untouched & barely lukewarm; watch smashed at 8:48 PM.'

"Think back! At 8:42 PM in the Grand Hall, I personally watched Chef Henri Laurent hand Arthur a signature dark-chocolate truffle—and Arthur carried it straight up to his locked Study!"

characters.detention: Searched from Harriet's Coat: A retired magistrate's badge, a miniature chemistry testing kit, and a note from Arthur: 'Harriet — Tonight I am finally exposing the 2008 cover-up. Watch those I trust most.'

dialogues.target: Say to Lady Evelyn Vance [after Exhibit F]:

characters.name: Margot Bell
characters.special: YOU ARE ON THE SHADOW TEAM! You are allied with Chef Henri Laurent and win ONLY if the Killer escapes indictment in the Final Verdict. Wake up with the Shadow Team during Blackout Phases.

exhibits.title: Exhibit A — Study Crime Scene Sketch (9:02 PM)
exhibits.html:
• Door & Window: Heavy oak double-door bolted from the inside; cliff window latched inside.
  • The Body: Lord Arthur Vance slumped across his desk blotter. First reached and rolled over by Chef Henri Laurent at 9:01 PM.
  • Initial Statement (9:01 PM): As guests rushed in, Chef Henri Laurent loudly claimed to see Arthur's "chalk-pale lips" and smell "bitter almonds from the spilled wine."
  • On the Desk: Unsigned New Will; a crystal wine glass; a single poured porcelain cup of chamomile tea (barely lukewarm by 9:02 PM); a broken pocket watch.
  • On the Floor: Shattered glass beside a heavy 5-lb brass counterweight in a pool of spilled liquid.

exhibits.title: Exhibit B — Arthur's Shattered Pocket Watch
exhibits.html:
• Make: Custom Vance Precision Gold Chronometer ("A.V. — Time Never Lies").
  • Condition: Crystal cracked; internal gears jammed from hitting the desk corner.
  • Frozen Time: 8:48 PM (12 minutes before the 9:00 PM blackout).
  • Witness Note: Chef Henri Laurent snapped the gold lid shut at 9:01 PM, claiming Arthur's watch "always ran twelve minutes slow."

exhibits.title: Exhibit C — Charred Audit Log ('H.L.' / 'M.B.')
exhibits.html:

-------------------------------------------------

exhibits.title: Exhibit D — Chronos Automaton, Wax Cylinder & Study Re-Inspection
exhibits.html:
• Phonograph Drum: Plays a removable brass wax cylinder at a scheduled minute. Currently set to 8:55 PM.
  • Release Cam: Drops a 5-lb brass counterweight at 9:00 PM (shifted 2 inches to strike the water carafe).
  • Cylinder Label: Reads "9:00 PM Gala Greeting" — hastily glued over a scratched-out title: "Memoir Draft — Confrontation."
  • Study Re-Inspection (Clear Light): The crystal wine glass on the desk is completely full & untouched; the shattered glass on the floor is a water carafe in clear, odorless liquid (zero wine, zero bitter-almond scent). Desk-blotter impressions confirm Arthur collapsed face-down, facing away from the door until Chef Henri Laurent rolled him over.

exhibits.html:

    • Lady Evelyn Vance: Director of Vance Charity Gala Fund (2006–2008)
    • Thomas Graves: Estate Steward & Keyholder, Ravenshollow (1999–present)
    • Harriet Vance-Cole: County Magistrate, Coastal District (2004–2008)
    • Chef Henri Laurent: Executive Chef, Le Chronomètre Paris (2006–2008)
    • Margot Bell: Cleared — No clearance or access to Archive Box #4 in 2008 (unrelated to the 2008 incident).
    • Father Silas Ward: Parish Treasurer, St. Jude's Coastal Parish (2005–2008)
  • Arthur's Horologist Journal (Nov 15): "A clockmaker whose own pocket watch loses a single second is a fraud. My gold chronometer is calibrated daily to the U.S. Naval Observatory signal. It has not drifted by half a second in eleven years."

exhibits.title: Exhibit F — Field Toxicology Report
exhibits.html:
• Red Wine (Dining Sideboard Decanter & Untouched Study Glass): Positive for Chloral Hydrate (non-lethal sleeping sedative). Arthur never drank it.
  • Residue on Arthur's Lips & Cuff: Positive for Concentrated Aconite (fast-acting, completely odorless cardiac poison; fatal in 2–3 minutes) — matching trace contact from a signature dark-chocolate truffle.
  • Floor Puddle: Plain spring water. Zero wine, zero bitter-almond odor.

exhibits.html:
Found crumpled on the basement stairs immediately after the blackout:

"9:00 PM sharp. Pull the main breaker. Don't let anyone see you. — E.V."

Slipped under the Library door during the blackout:

"Check the Dining & Sideboard! Someone wiped down the Bordeaux decanter left on the sideboard with an almond-scented handkerchief right before 9:00 PM."

prologue.label: PROLOGUE — 9:00 PM
prologue.sub: Read aloud (or click Read Aloud) to set the scene at Ravenshollow Manor.
prologue.html:
Welcome to Ravenshollow Manor. Outside, a violent November nor'easter has washed out the wooden bridge to the mainland, and the telephone lines are dead. You are guests of billionaire clockmaker Lord Arthur Vance (72).

At 8:45 PM, Arthur retired alone to his second-floor Study to fetch his New Will, bolting the heavy oak door from the inside. At 8:55 PM, guests in the Grand Hall heard Arthur shouting from upstairs: "You've gone too far! I'm calling the police as soon as the lines are back!"

At 9:00 PM sharp, as the Grand Astronomical Clock struck nine, the backup generator died—plunging the manor into darkness for 15 seconds. A sharp crack and heavy thud echoed from the Study. When the lights returned at 9:01 PM, you broke down the bolted door—and found Arthur Vance dead at his desk.

Father Silas Ward (#13)

Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"There is no bullet wound. It was poison! The moment the lights came back on at 9:01, I saw Arthur's chalk-pale lips and smelled that unmistakable bitter-almond scent from the spilled wine. He died right around nine."
Thomas Graves (#3)
"Begging your pardon, but when I stepped beside the desk, I noticed Lord Arthur's pocket watch had smashed on the corner—its hands were stopped at 8:48."
Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"Ah, yes, I closed the lid so it wouldn't upset everyone. Arthur's watch always ran twelve minutes slow—he told me so himself just yesterday."
Harriet Vance-Cole (#8)
"Slow or not, the New Will is still on his desk—unsigned. Whoever wanted Arthur dead before 9:00 PM is standing in this room."

revealHtml:
The Truth Behind the Last Chime (RV-6711)

The Killer: Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
The Accomplice (Shadow Team): Margot Bell (#10)
The Inspector: Harriet Vance-Cole (#8)

Arthur Vance did not die at 9:00 PM. He died at 8:48 PM—alone behind a bolted door—from concentrated Aconite hidden in the signature dark-chocolate truffle handed to him by Chef Henri Laurent (#9) at 8:42 PM. At 9:01 PM, Chef Henri Laurent rushed to the desk first, pocketing the signature dark-chocolate truffle and later ditching a botanical-smudged handkerchief down the upstairs laundry chute.

Lady Evelyn Vance (#1) spiked the red wine with harmless sleeping powder, which Arthur never touched. The 8:55 PM argument was a pre-recorded brass wax cylinder played by the Chronos Automaton, and the 9:00 PM crash was the counterweight smashing the water carafe while blackmailed accomplice Margot Bell (#10) cut the generator breaker for 15 seconds.

The 4-Pillar Proof: (1) Arthur's pocket watch froze at 8:48 PM and his Horologist Journal proves it never lost a second; (2) The wine was untouched and Arthur died of odorless Aconite from the signature dark-chocolate truffle; (3) Chef Henri Laurent slipped up in Act I by claiming to see Arthur's pale lips (Arthur was face-down!) and smell bitter almonds from spilled wine (it was odorless water!); (4) Exhibit C flagged both "H.L." and "M.B.", but Exhibit E clears Margot Bell (no 2008 access) and ties Chef Henri Laurent directly to 2008 Paris Kitchen — Fatal Allergen Cover-Up — Executive Chef, Le Chronomètre Paris (2006–2008)!
